                                                           2   I.       STATEMENT OF ISSUES (Civil L.R. 7-4(a)(3))

                                                           3         1. Whether AmeriSave’s claims are barred by the statute of limitations, where its
                                                           4            own pleadings admit RingCentral disclosed the alleged “fundamental limitation”
                                                           5            on October 20, 2021, and AmeriSave immediately reverted to its prior system.
                                                           6            (Amended Counterclaims (“Am. Countercl.”) ¶¶ 24, 33–34.)

                                                           8            “discovered” fraud in 2023 despite admitting knowledge of both alleged injury
                                                           9            and its purported cause in 2021.
                                                       10            3. Whether AmeriSave’s Amended Counterclaim impermissibly contradicts its
                                                       11               prior judicial admissions, in violation of Fed. R. Civ. P. 15, by asserting a new
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12               narrative inconsistent with facts it previously pleaded. Specifically, AmeriSave’s

AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14               regarding the timing of knowledge and injury. The Amended Counterclaim now
                                                       15               alleges “discovery” of alleged fraud in 2023, but the original Counterclaim and
                                                       16               the Amended Counterclaim both admit that RingCentral disclosed the
                                                       17               “fundamental limitation” on October 20, 2021, and AmeriSave immediately
                                                       18               reverted to its prior system.
                                                       19            4. Whether AmeriSave states any fraud based claim with sufficient particularity
                                                       20               under Fed. R. Civ. P. 9(b), where it identifies no specific false statement, speaker,
                                                       21               timing, or contemporaneous falsity.
                                                       22            5. Whether the economic loss doctrine bars AmeriSave’s tort claims, which seek

                                                       27      II.      INTRODUCTION AND PERTINENT ALLEGATIONS

                                                       28               The Amended Counterclaim fails and should be dismissed with prejudice.

                                                                                                            1               CASE NO: 4:25-cv-08694-WHO
                                                                                        MOTION TO DISMISS AMENDED COUNTERCLAIM
                                                            1            AmeriSave alleges pre-Master Services Agreement discussions in March–April 2021 and an

                                                           2   executed April 2021 Master Services Agreement (“MSA”). AmeriSave further alleges that on October

                                                           3   20, 2021, RingCentral disclosed a “fundamental limitation” preventing the required call pace agreed

                                                           4   expected from the MSA, resulting in AmeriSave reverting back to its prior telephony system – walking

                                                           5   away from the MSA, shortly thereafter. The Amended Counterclaim adds names of certain

                                                           6   RingCentral personnel and, for the first time, asserts AmeriSave did not “discover” a basis for civil

                                                           7   liability until 2023. (Am. Countercl. ¶¶ 24, 33–34, 18, 31–32, 43, 54, 65.) AmeriSave’s new allegation

                                                           8   that it did not “discover” a basis for tort and contract liability until 2023 contradicts its earlier judicial

                                                           9   admissions that RingCentral disclosed the alleged “fundamental limitation” on October 20, 2021,

                                                       10      which served as the catalyst for AmeriSave to promptly revert to its prior system. (Am. Countercl. ¶¶

                                                       11      24, 33–34.) The 2021 disclosure and actions taken in response undermine the purported two year delay
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      in AmeriSave “discovering” in 2023 the basis for tort and contract-related liability. See, Beasley v.
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13      Lucky Stores, Inc., 400 F.Supp.3d 942, 958-959 (N.D. Cal. 2019), and, Fox v. Ethicon Endo-Surgery,
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      Inc., 35 Cal.4th 797, 808 (2005). All claims are time-barred.

                                                            1          Even if the claims were timely, each fails independently under Fed. R. Civ. P. 9(b) and

                                                           5   III.   ARGUMENT

                                                           6          A.      Fed. R. Civ. P. 15 and Judicial Admissions Bar the Amended Theory

                                                           7          AmeriSave’s amendment serves as an impermissible contradiction under Fed. R. Civ. P. 15.

                                                           8   (See, FN 1, supra.) The Amended Counterclaim does not clarify or supplement its original allegations

                                                           9   – it repudiates them.

                                                       10             AmeriSave’s effort to sustain its untimely Counterclaim filed in response to RingCentral’s

                                                       11      Complaint (Court Doc. 1), is legally untenable because the delayed discovery rule turns on when a
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      claimant has reason to suspect wrongdoing—not when it later chooses to label the same conduct as
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13      “fraud” and/or claims arising from contract. (See, Section III.B., infra.) The Amended Counterclaim
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      now alleges “discovery” of fraud in 2023, but the original Counterclaim and the Amended

                                                       15      Counterclaim both admit that RingCentral disclosed the alleged “fundamental limitation” on October

                                                       16      20, 2021, and AmeriSave immediately reverted to its prior system. (Am. Countercl. ¶¶ 24, 33–34.)

                                                       17      Under controlling California law, the 2021 knowledge triggered “inquiry notice” as a matter of law,

                                                       18      which forecloses AmeriSave from asserting that it “did not discover” wrongdoing until 2023.

                                                       19             The Ninth Circuit forbids claimants from contradicting prior pleadings to manufacture

                                                       20      timeliness. Reddy v. Litton Industries, Inc., 912 F.2d 291, 296 (9th Cir. 1990) (affirming denial of

                                                       21      leave to amend where proposed amendment would be inconsistent with prior complaint). The Court

                                                       22      should disregard the contradictory allegations, treat the original admissions as binding, and dismiss

                                                       23      with prejudice. (See Footnote 1, supra.) “Factual assertions in pleadings … are considered judicial

                                                       24      admissions” and are conclusively binding unless properly withdrawn or amended. American Title Ins.

                                                       25      Co. v. Lacelaw Corp., 861 F.2d 224, 226 (9th Cir. 1988).

                                                       26
                                                       27                                                                          disclosure. (¶¶ 18, 31–32,
                                                                                                                                   43, 54, 65)

                                                                                        MOTION TO DISMISS AMENDED COUNTERCLAIM
                                                            1          To the extent AmeriSave’s amendments conflict with the MSA, contemporaneous

                                                           2   communications, or its own prior pleadings, those contradictions do not save the claims at Fed. R. Civ.

                                                           3   P. 12. AmeriSave cannot contradict its earlier factual theory to avoid dismissal. The Ninth Circuit’s

                                                           4   Rule 15 and judicial admission doctrines bar that tactic.

                                                           5          The Amended Counterclaim remains time barred, fails Fed. R. Civ. P. 9(b), seeks only

                                                           6   economic losses barred by law, contradicts prior admissions, and depends on reliance expressly

                                                           7   foreclosed by the MSA. Amendment was therefore futile and undertaken in an effort to plead around

                                                           8   dispositive facts. RingCentral requests this Court disregard the new “delayed discovery” allegations

                                                           9   as sham and treat the original admissions as binding. Dismissal with prejudice is warranted.

                                                       10             B.      Statute of Limitations Bars All Claims

                                                       11             To invoke delayed discovery, a claimant must plead specific facts showing (1) the time and
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      manner of discovery and (2) the inability to discover earlier despite reasonable diligence. Conclusory
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13      allegations do not suffice. Beasley, supra, 400 F.Supp.3d 958-959, Yamauchi v. Cotterman, 84
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      F.Supp.3d 993, 1011 (N.D. Cal. 2015). The Northern District has consistently applied this two-part

                                                       15      test, emphasizing that plaintiffs bear “the burden on the plaintiff to show diligence; conclusory

                                                       16      allegations will not withstand” a motion to dismiss (Beasley, 400 F.Supp.3d 942). “Formal averments

                                                       17      or general conclusions to the effect that the facts were not discovered until a stated date, and that

                                                       18      plaintiff could not reasonably have made an earlier discovery, are useless” (Al-Ahmed v. Twitter, Inc.,

                                                       19      648 F.Supp.3d 1140, 1156 (N.D. Cal. 2023), citing, Chione v. Medtronic, Inc., No. 14-CV-01043-

                                                       20      BAS RBB, 2015 WL 2151889, at *4 (S.D. Cal. May 7, 2015), quoting Anderson v. Brouwer, 99 Cal.

                                                       21      App. 3d 176, 182 (1979)); and see Eidson v. Medtronic, Inc., 981 F.Supp.2d 868, 892-894 (N.D. Cal.
